newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end mixed on China cancellation talk.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end mixed on China cancellation talk.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended mixed with most contracts down amid rampant rumors China cancelled 450,000 tonnes of South American and Indian soymeal purchases, traders said.
"It opened higher then fizzled led by meal on the China rumors. It's been all over the place," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.

Brazilian sources said they could not confirm the cancellations but said it was conceivable China would resell soymeal due to the recent price action. China could profit by reselling soymeal at higher prices.
"It makes sense from a business point of view that they actually might do it," a Brazilian trader said.
CBOT sources cited recent reports that China's ports were clogged with soymeal and domestic prices were falling.
Soybeans ended three cents per bushel lower to two cents higher with March down three at $7.83.
USDA weekly export figures of 402,900 tonnes were in line with expectations and did not have much effect on the market.
Some sources suggested U.S. soybean exports would pick up in the next few weeks because Brazil's ports were backed up and exporters were having trouble loading for spot shipment.

Brazil's port of Paranagua began loading the first of the 1996-97 soybean harvest this week but delays in harvesting in Parana state meant there was not enough product to cover commitments, traders there said.
One trader said 400,000 tonnes of soybeans had been committed for spot delivery but stocks were at 14,000 tonnes.

On the day, Cargill Inc bought four million bushels May and 1.5 million bushels March. Refco Inc bought 4.5 million May and sold 2.5 million May and 2.5 million March. Local traders sold at least seven million bushels on the day.
In options trade, USA Trading bought 200 March $8.00 calls at 3/8 to 3/4 cent. E.D. and F. Man International bought 100 May $8.00 calls at 20 cents, traders said.
